principles: Keep cli-engine.ts as the compatibility boundary until downstream consumers migrate.
Move cohesive helper groups only; do not combine unrelated lifecycle dispatch work into this story.
Gate-consumed facts must remain mechanically verified by existing contract scripts and focused smokes.
Prefer small modules that preserve imports/types over broad rewrites.
drivers: cli-engine.ts god-file pressure is high but gate behavior is production-sensitive.
Parallel story B-74a0 may add packages/main/src/cli modules, so this story should create disjoint files under that directory.
Owner lease and reviewer readonly semantics must remain fail-closed.

options.name: A: Extract four focused runtime/gate helper modules with compatibility re-exports
pros: Matches the Round 3 execution plan exactly.
Keeps the public cli-engine export surface stable.
Allows focused ownership contract smoke coverage.
cons: Requires careful import wiring because helpers share command policy and story owner lease types.
Does not reduce lifecycle dispatch complexity yet.

options.name: B: Leave ownership gates in cli-engine and only extract root/activity helpers
pros: Lower immediate risk around owner lease behavior.
cons: Does not address the largest high-risk section in cli-engine.
Leaves reviewer readonly and owner lease logic tangled with run wrapper.

options.name: C: Move full run wrapper and lifecycle dispatch together now
pros: Maximizes line-count reduction in one story.
Could create a cleaner CLI shell quickly.
cons: Combines Round 3 and Round 4 risks and conflicts with the staged plan.
Harder to isolate regressions in INIT_CHECK and recover_evidence dispatch.

chosen: A: Extract four focused runtime/gate helper modules with compatibility re-exports
rationale: Choose the focused Round 3 extraction because it reduces cli-engine size while keeping gate semantics, exports, and lifecycle dispatch stable for parallel integration.

preMortem.scenario: Owner-gated command starts bypassing the story owner lease.
preMortem.trigger: Effective ownership class helper changes a null/invalid policy into an allow path.
preMortem.consequence: Foreign sessions can mutate story state and corrupt evidence.
preMortem.mitigation: Keep fail-closed null semantics, run command ownership contract smoke, and verify process fact contract.

preMortem.scenario: Read-only reviewer mode accidentally writes hooks/activity/lease state before blocking.
preMortem.trigger: Reviewer readonly guard is moved after pre-command hooks or owner lease enforcement.
preMortem.consequence: Advisory reviewers can mutate state despite read-only mode.
preMortem.mitigation: Preserve call ordering and add/keep smoke assertions for read-only rejection before mutation.

preMortem.scenario: Activity logging loses main-root fallback after DONE worktree cleanup.
preMortem.trigger: Root resolution helper prefers cwd after worktree deletion instead of saved fallback.
preMortem.consequence: Post-command activity logs vanish or write to the wrong root.
preMortem.mitigation: Extract root helpers without changing fallback order and cover with build plus validate commands.

preMortem.scenario: Parallel merge with B-74a0 causes imports to diverge.
preMortem.trigger: Both stories edit cli-engine imports and create files under src/cli.
preMortem.consequence: Merge conflict or duplicate helper definitions during DONE integration.
preMortem.mitigation: Use disjoint module filenames and keep compatibility exports in cli-engine.
